findings: Cost-cap control exists on paper but is inert by default: the delegation scope template ships maximum_cost: null (docs/authority.md, docs/phase-1/0001, docs/security/0002), and the recovery bound is conditional — 'per delegation maximum_cost if set' (docs/security/0001 §11.1) — with no documented default cap or enforcement wiring.

No cost telemetry exists: the observability metrics (docs/operations/0001-observability.md §6) cover totals, denials, recovery, parallelism, latency and integrity, but have no token or currency-cost dimension, so unit economics (cost per task, per run, per finding) are not computable from the audit ledger today.

Cost/latency behaviour of real parallel spawns is explicitly recorded as UNKNOWN (docs/phase-4/0001 §13; docs/phase-4/0002 §4 gap table) — the only live unit-economics-adjacent data point is the INT-11 timing sample.

Dominant cost drivers are per-spawn fixed context payload, fan-out width, and retry/rework multipliers; the six control-plane gates are code-enforced and deterministic, so their marginal cost is CPU/IO, not model tokens.

Live INT-11 baseline: three parallel read-only children settled in 13s (nova), 34s (cfo), 52s (kai) — makespan 52s vs ~99s serial (~47% wall-clock compression with zero token savings); a first dispatch batch was abandoned after HTTP 429, roughly doubling that batch's token spend, and no backoff/scheduling exists (REC-G4-1 deferred).

Bounded worst-case multipliers: max_attempts=1 per diagnosed cause plus max_rework_cycles=2 gives up to ~4x subtask executions per subtask; mandatory BadSector review + independent verification + Human confirmation for financial commitments (security spec §16.1) adds further full specialist passes — every financial-commitment decision carries this unquantified governance overhead.

Existing cost levers already in the presets: minimum-specialist-set routing (no blanket fan-out; a pricing objective routes to [cfo, kai] per AEF-3/P4I-03), 64 KiB agent-instruction cap per role preset, tool-result pruning (8 KiB threshold -> 4096+1024 chars), read-only specialist scopes (no execution surface), and parallel makespan compression.

Fixed governance payload dominates small read-only tasks: each specialist spawn carries the always-on TOKEN-ECONOMY v2.4 policy block, role files and tool schemas before any task work begins — for a task like this one, the fixed per-spawn cost exceeds the task-specific context.

risks: Unbounded-spend exposure: with maximum_cost null and no cost telemetry, a parallel batch amplified by repeated 429-driven redispatch can multiply token spend with no circuit breaker beyond the attempt/rework caps.
Rate-limit exposure converts directly into abandoned batches (wasted tokens) and user-facing delay; REC-G4-1 (bounded backoff) is deferred, not implemented.

Scaling decisions are being made blind: fan-out width and routing (e.g., 2-3 children per objective) are chosen without any cost signal, so there is no basis for a cost-based trade-off against latency.

findings: F (web): Agentic-AI / multi-agent orchestration is the fastest-growing enterprise AI segment; analyst estimates diverge widely on size (e.g., Mordor: ~USD 6.96B 2025 to ~USD 57.42B 2031; MarketsandMarkets: ~USD 19.33B 2026 to ~USD 205.88B 2033, ~40% CAGR) — treat as directional ~30-40% CAGR growth, not as a single verified figure.

I: The trend has shifted from single-agent to orchestrated multi-agent systems; competing frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, Microsoft Agent Framework, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK) are maturing into enterprise production, so differentiation is moving from agent capability to coordination, control, and trust.

I: The strongest trend alignment for this project is governance-as-bottleneck: Gartner (via secondary citations) predicts >40% of agentic-AI projects canceled by 2027 citing escalating costs, unclear ROI, and weak risk controls — exactly the failure modes a fail-closed authority/delegation/audit control plane addresses. Primary market angle: trust layer for multi-agent orchestration.

I: Second demand driver is security and agent identity: ~80% of organizations reportedly see agents act beyond intended scope; a non-human-identity / least-privilege-agent vendor category is emerging (Okta, CyberArk, Microsoft agent-identity moves; CSA NHI governance whitepaper). The project's capability-≠-permission-≠-authority model and scope-subset delegation map directly onto this nascent category.

I: Project-specific relevance: the workspace already implements the governance primitives the market lacks (three-layer enforcement per docs/architecture.md, delegation registry with expiry/revocation per docs/authority.md, risk/evidence/conflict gates, review-only BadSector, append-only audit). It should be positioned against the governance gap, not against orchestration-framework features.

findings: README.md documents architecture, three enforcement layers, project structure, phase status, and human decisions (D1-D7) but contains no value-proposition statement; the draft below fills that gap and is intended to sit directly under the H1/title block.

Draft two-sentence value proposition (verbatim, ready to paste): "This repository is the control plane for a multi-agent system built on DeepSeek Harness: one coordinating orchestrator and seven peer specialists - operations, engineering, finance, research, social, adversarial review, and writing - bound by explicit role definitions and a three-layer enforcement model that keeps capability, permission, and authority strictly separate. Phase 1 delivers the documented architecture - ADRs, a threat model, and design and test plans - alongside a working skeleton of JSON Schema contracts, state and audit integrity helpers, and a validation test suite, with every gate fail-closed, all authority traced to the Human, and subdelegation denied by default."

Every factual claim in the draft traces to repository sources: peer structure and no-specialist-manages-another (README.md, docs/architecture.md §1); three enforcement layers (README.md, architecture.md §2); capability != permission != authority (docs/authority.md §1); Human as sole authority source and fail-closed gates (architecture.md §3-4, authority.md §2); subdelegation DENY BY DEFAULT (authority.md §2 and README.md fixed V1 defaults); Phase 1B deliverables (README.md phase status table; tests/, state/helpers/, audit/helpers/, schemas/ confirmed present in the tree).
The DeepSeek Harness version pin (0.1.1-rc.2) was deliberately kept out of the value proposition: it is already stated twice in README.md and pin text is maintenance-sensitive.
